claim: The mouse RPB1 CTD is composed of 52 heptapeptide repeats with consensus amino-acid sequence YSPTSPS.
source: Mouse RPB1 CTD is composed of 52 heptapeptide repeats with consensus amino-acid sequence YSPTSPS, which is represented 21 times at the most proximal CTD region.
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 1a which displays the sequence composition of the mouse RPB1 CTD.

claim: The consensus sequence YSPTSPS is represented 21 times at the most proximal CTD region.
source: Mouse RPB1 CTD is composed of 52 heptapeptide repeats with consensus amino-acid sequence YSPTSPS, which is represented 21 times at the most proximal CTD region.
evidence: Directly stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1a.

claim: Non-consensus amino acids are enriched at the distal CTD region.
source: Non-consensus amino acids are enriched for at the distal region.
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 1a which displays the distribution of non-consensus residues.

claim: The most abundant non-consensus residues in the mouse CTD are lysines, all found at heptad position 7 (K7).
source: Most abundant non-consensus residues are lysines, all found at heptad position 7 (K7; represented in red).
evidence: Explicitly stated in text and visualized in Figure 1a.

claim: The number of non-canonical K7-containing repeats increases from zero in yeast to one, three and eight repeats in C. elegans, D. melanogaster and vertebrates, respectively.
source: The number of non-canonical K7-containing repeats increases from zero in yeast to one, three and eight repeats in C. elegans, D. melanogaster and vertebrates, respectively (Figure 1b).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 1b which displays sequence alignment across species.

claim: CTD-K7 residues can be acetylated.
source: Previous work has shown that non-canonical CTD-K7 residues can be acetylated, and that CTD-K7ac is associated with transcriptional pausing at epidermal growth factor (EGF)-inducible genes in mouse fibroblasts (Schroeder et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior published work.

claim: CTD-K7ac is associated with transcriptional pausing at epidermal growth factor (EGF)-inducible genes in mouse fibroblasts.
source: Previous work has shown that non-canonical CTD-K7 residues can be acetylated, and that CTD-K7ac is associated with transcriptional pausing at epidermal growth factor (EGF)-inducible genes in mouse fibroblasts (Schroeder et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior published work.

claim: Mutation of CTD-K7 residues to S7 is compatible with cell viability in mouse NIH-3T3 fibroblasts.
source: We produced viable mouse NIH-3T3 fibroblast lines that express each of the four constructs and show stable YFP-RPB1 expression for more than one month in culture and after several passages under α-amanitin selection.
evidence: Demonstrated by successful generation and maintenance of stable cell lines expressing K7-to-S7 mutant constructs.

claim: Mutation of K7-to-S7 residues is compatible with normal global levels of serine phosphorylation.
source: Western blot analyses of CTD phosphorylation using highly specific antibodies against S5p, S7p and S2p (Brookes et al., 2012; Stock et al., 2007), detect hyperphosphorylated (II0) RPB1 in untransfected NIH-3T3, wild-type 8K and 0K mutant cells, showing that mutation of K7-to-S7 residues is compatible with normal global levels of serine phosphorylation.
evidence: Demonstrated by western blot data shown in Figure 2b and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mutation of CTD-K7 residues does not affect the typical RNAPII nucleoplasmic distribution.
source: To examine the effect of K7-to-S7 mutation on the subcellular localization of RPB1, we used confocal microscopy and YFP fluorescence to detect YFP-RPB1 fusion proteins and found that the typical RNAPII nucleoplasmic distribution is unaffected by K7-to-S7 mutations (Figure 2c; e.g. Xie et al., 2006).
evidence: Demonstrated by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: CTD-K7 residues are mono-methylated in vivo in mouse fibroblasts.
source: K7me1 and K7me2 are detected in NIH-3T3 and in 8K cell lines, both of which express a CTD with eight K7 residues, but not in the 0K mutant cell line, where all K7 residues are mutated to S7. These results confirm the specificity of the K7me1 and K7me2 antibodies to CTD-K7 modifications. The single band in NIH-3T3 and in 8K cell lines shows lack of cross-reactivity to other NIH-3T3 proteins (Figure 3—figure supplement 1a). These results demonstrate the existence of in vivo methylation of non-canonical K7 residues of the CTD in mouse fibroblasts.
evidence: Demonstrated by western blot data in Figure 3d showing K7me1 detection in 8K but not 0K cell lines.

claim: CTD-K7 residues are di-methylated in vivo in mouse fibroblasts.
source: K7me1 and K7me2 are detected in NIH-3T3 and in 8K cell lines, both of which express a CTD with eight K7 residues, but not in the 0K mutant cell line, where all K7 residues are mutated to S7. These results confirm the specificity of the K7me1 and K7me2 antibodies to CTD-K7 modifications. The single band in NIH-3T3 and in 8K cell lines shows lack of cross-reactivity to other NIH-3T3 proteins (Figure 3—figure supplement 1a). These results demonstrate the existence of in vivo methylation of non-canonical K7 residues of the CTD in mouse fibroblasts.
evidence: Demonstrated by western blot data in Figure 3d showing K7me2 detection in 8K but not 0K cell lines.

claim: K7me1 and K7me2 antibodies detect the hypophosphorylated RPB1 form.
source: Interestingly, we found that both the K7me1 and K7me2 antibodies detect the hypophosphorylated RPB1 and YFP-RPB1 bands (Figure 3d).
evidence: Demonstrated by western blot data in Figure 3d showing K7me1 and K7me2 detection at the IIa (hypophosphorylated) band.

claim: Multiple CTD-K7 residues are simultaneously mono-methylated in mammalian cells.
source: Mono- and di-methylation were identified in total cell extracts from the 1K cell line. The intensities of mono- and di-methylation increase in the 3K line, indicating that several lysine residues are mono- and di-methylated in the same CTD. The level of mono-methylation increases further in the 8K-cell line, showing abundant mono-methylation of the CTD in vivo.
evidence: Demonstrated by western blot data in Figure 3e showing increasing K7me1 signal with increasing number of K7 residues.

claim: Multiple CTD-K7 residues are simultaneously di-methylated in mammalian cells.
source: Mono- and di-methylation were identified in total cell extracts from the 1K cell line. The intensities of mono- and di-methylation increase in the 3K line, indicating that several lysine residues are mono- and di-methylated in the same CTD.
evidence: Demonstrated by western blot data in Figure 3e showing K7me2 signal in 1K and 3K cell lines.

claim: Not all eight CTD lysine-7 residues are simultaneously di-methylated.
source: In contrast, the di-methylation levels remain similar between the 8K and 3K lines, suggesting that not all eight CTD lysine-7 residues are simultaneously di-methylated, and reflecting a possible preference for di-methylation of the K residues conserved between mammals and invertebrates, which are present in the 3K construct.
evidence: Inferred from western blot data in Figure 3e showing similar K7me2 levels in 3K and 8K cell lines.

claim: CTD-K7 di-methylation is conserved in C. elegans.
source: K7me2 is also detected in whole protein extracts from adult Caenorhabditis elegans worm, Drosophila melanogaster embryos, and human HEK293 cells, in western blotting analysis (Figure 3f, Figure 3—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: Demonstrated by western blot data in Figure 3f showing K7me2 detection in C. elegans extracts.

claim: CTD-K7 di-methylation is conserved in D. melanogaster.
source: K7me2 is also detected in whole protein extracts from adult Caenorhabditis elegans worm, Drosophila melanogaster embryos, and human HEK293 cells, in western blotting analysis (Figure 3f, Figure 3—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: Demonstrated by western blot data in Figure 3f showing K7me2 detection in D. melanogaster extracts.

claim: CTD-K7 di-methylation is conserved in human cells.
source: K7me2 is also detected in whole protein extracts from adult Caenorhabditis elegans worm, Drosophila melanogaster embryos, and human HEK293 cells, in western blotting analysis (Figure 3f, Figure 3—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: Demonstrated by western blot data in Figure 3f showing K7me2 detection in human HEK293 cells.

claim: CTD-K7 mono-methylation occurs in human cells.
source: K7me1 also occurs in human cells and C. elegans, but is not easily detected in extracts from D. melanogaster embryos, suggesting that di-methylation may be a more prevalent methylation mark.
evidence: Demonstrated by western blot data in Figure 3f showing K7me1 detection in human cells.

claim: CTD-K7 mono-methylation occurs in C. elegans.
source: K7me1 also occurs in human cells and C. elegans, but is not easily detected in extracts from D. melanogaster embryos, suggesting that di-methylation may be a more prevalent methylation mark.
evidence: Demonstrated by western blot data in Figure 3f showing K7me1 detection in C. elegans.

claim: CTD-K7 methylation is associated with early stages of the transcription cycle.
source: The observation that mono- and di-methylation of CTD-K7 residues is detected primarily in the hypophosphorylated (faster-migrating) forms of RPB1 (Figure 3d) suggests that CTD methylation is associated with early stages of the transcription cycle.
evidence: Inferred from western blot data in Figure 3d and supported by additional experiments in Figure 4.

claim: Immunodetection of K7me1 and K7me2 is only minimally affected by CTD phosphorylation.
source: We find that the detection of K7 methylation remains specific to the hypophosphorylated RPB1 after treatment of immunoblots with alkaline phosphatase, showing only a minor increase in the detection of K7me1 and K7me2 at intermediately phosphorylated forms, in conditions that fully abrogate detection of phosphorylated epitopes (e.g. S5p; see also Stock et al., 2007). Therefore, immunodetection of K7me1 and K7me2 is only minimally affected by CTD phosphorylation, suggesting that K7me1 and K7me2 modifications are depleted from elongation-competent hyperphosphorylated RPB1 complexes.
evidence: Demonstrated by alkaline phosphatase treatment experiment shown in Figure 4a.

claim: K7me1 and K7me2 modifications are depleted from elongation-competent hyperphosphorylated RPB1 complexes.
source: Therefore, immunodetection of K7me1 and K7me2 is only minimally affected by CTD phosphorylation, suggesting that K7me1 and K7me2 modifications are depleted from elongation-competent hyperphosphorylated RPB1 complexes.
evidence: Inferred from alkaline phosphatase treatment data in Figure 4a and flavopiridol treatment data in Figure 4b.

claim: K7me1 and K7me2 levels are only minimally increased by flavopiridol treatment.
source: We find that K7me1 and K7me2 levels are only minimally increased by flavopiridol treatment (Figure 4b), consistent with both modifications being associated with pre-elongation stages of transcription.
evidence: Demonstrated by western blot data in Figure 4b showing K7me1 and K7me2 levels before and after flavopiridol treatment.

claim: K7me1 and K7me2 are associated with pre-elongation stages of transcription.
source: We find that K7me1 and K7me2 levels are only minimally increased by flavopiridol treatment (Figure 4b), consistent with both modifications being associated with pre-elongation stages of transcription.
evidence: Inferred from flavopiridol treatment data in Figure 4b.

claim: K7me1 and K7me2 are concentrated in punctate nucleoplasmic domains.
source: We find K7me1 and K7me2 concentrated in punctate nucleoplasmic domains, absent from nucleoli and regions of heterochromatin.
evidence: Demonstrated by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4c.

claim: K7me1 and K7me2 are absent from nucleoli.
source: We find K7me1 and K7me2 concentrated in punctate nucleoplasmic domains, absent from nucleoli and regions of heterochromatin.
evidence: Demonstrated by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4c.

claim: K7me1 and K7me2 are absent from regions of heterochromatin.
source: We find K7me1 and K7me2 concentrated in punctate nucleoplasmic domains, absent from nucleoli and regions of heterochromatin.
evidence: Demonstrated by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4c.

claim: K7me1 and K7me2 are highly enriched at promoters of active genes.
source: Inspection of ChIP-seq profiles at single genes shows that K7me1 and K7me2 are highly enriched at promoters of active genes (Eed, Rpl13, and Tuba1a), and are detected at lower levels beyond transcription end sites (Figure 5a).
evidence: Demonstrated by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 5a and genome-wide analysis in Figure 5e.

claim: K7 methylation and acetylation are not detected at inactive genes.
source: K7 methylation and acetylation, and other RNAPII modifications, are not detected at inactive genes (e.g. Myf5 gene).
evidence: Demonstrated by ChIP-seq data in Figure 5a showing absence of signal at the Myf5 gene.

claim: K7me1 and K7me2 are more tightly localized to gene promoters than K7ac.
source: In summary, we find that K7me1 and K7me2 are more tightly localized to gene promoters than K7ac, suggesting association with the earliest stages of transcription.
evidence: Inferred from ChIP-seq profiles in Figure 5a and average profiles in Figure 5e.

claim: A total of 6962 gene promoters are positive for K7me1.
source: A total of 6962, 8265 and 8312 gene promoters were classified as positive for K7me1, K7me2 and K7ac, respectively.
evidence: Determined by computational analysis of ChIP-seq data using BCP peak finder.

claim: A total of 8265 gene promoters are positive for K7me2.
source: A total of 6962, 8265 and 8312 gene promoters were classified as positive for K7me1, K7me2 and K7ac, respectively.
evidence: Determined by computational analysis of ChIP-seq data using BCP peak finder.

claim: A total of 8312 gene promoters are positive for K7ac.
source: A total of 6962, 8265 and 8312 gene promoters were classified as positive for K7me1, K7me2 and K7ac, respectively.
evidence: Determined by computational analysis of ChIP-seq data using BCP peak finder.

claim: The vast majority of genes positive for K7me1, K7me2, or K7ac are positive for all three marks (n = 6398).
source: The vast majority of these genes are (i) positive for all three marks (n = 6398; Figure 5b), (ii) also marked by S5p, S7p, S2p and 8WG16 (Figure 5c), and (iii) transcriptionally active at the messenger RNA (mRNA) level (Figure 5d).
evidence: Demonstrated by Venn diagram analysis in Figure 5b.

claim: Genes positive for K7me1, K7me2, and K7ac are also marked by S5p, S7p, S2p and 8WG16.
source: The vast majority of these genes are (i) positive for all three marks (n = 6398; Figure 5b), (ii) also marked by S5p, S7p, S2p and 8WG16 (Figure 5c), and (iii) transcriptionally active at the messenger RNA (mRNA) level (Figure 5d).
evidence: Demonstrated by analysis in Figure 5c.

claim: Genes positive for K7me1, K7me2, and K7ac are transcriptionally active at the mRNA level.
source: The vast majority of these genes are (i) positive for all three marks (n = 6398; Figure 5b), (ii) also marked by S5p, S7p, S2p and 8WG16 (Figure 5c), and (iii) transcriptionally active at the messenger RNA (mRNA) level (Figure 5d).
evidence: Demonstrated by mRNA expression analysis in Figure 5d.

claim: K7me1 and K7me2 do not mark poised RNAPII at polycomb repressed genes.
source: Consistent with the specificity of K7me1 and K7me2 to expressed genes, we found that K7me1 and K7me2 do not mark poised RNAPII at PRCr genes marked by H3K27me3 and H2Aub1 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2a and 2b) and that they are associated with promoters marked by H3K4me3 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2c).
evidence: Demonstrated by analysis in Figure 5—figure supplement 2a and 2b.

claim: K7me1 and K7me2 are associated with promoters marked by H3K4me3.
source: Consistent with the specificity of K7me1 and K7me2 to expressed genes, we found that K7me1 and K7me2 do not mark poised RNAPII at PRCr genes marked by H3K27me3 and H2Aub1 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2a and 2b) and that they are associated with promoters marked by H3K4me3 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2c).
evidence: Demonstrated by analysis in Figure 5—figure supplement 2c.

claim: K7me1 and K7me2 are sharply enriched at the TSS.
source: The novel CTD modifications K7me1 and K7me2 are sharply enriched at the TSS. These profiles are very similar to that of S7p while, in contrast, K7ac is more broadly localized up- and downstream of the TSS.
evidence: Demonstrated by average occupancy profiles in Figure 5e.

claim: K7ac is more broadly localized up- and downstream of the TSS compared to K7me1 and K7me2.
source: These profiles are very similar to that of S7p while, in contrast, K7ac is more broadly localized up- and downstream of the TSS.
evidence: Demonstrated by average occupancy profiles in Figure 5e.

claim: mRNA levels are most strongly correlated with S2p levels at TES of active genes (Spearman's correlation coefficient 0.62).
source: We find that mRNA levels are most strongly correlated with S2p levels at TES of active genes (Spearman's correlation coefficient 0.62), followed by promoter K7ac (0.55) and S7p (0.49; Figure 6a).
evidence: Determined by correlation analysis shown in Figure 6a.

claim: mRNA levels correlate with promoter K7ac (Spearman's correlation coefficient 0.55).
source: We find that mRNA levels are most strongly correlated with S2p levels at TES of active genes (Spearman's correlation coefficient 0.62), followed by promoter K7ac (0.55) and S7p (0.49; Figure 6a).
evidence: Determined by correlation analysis shown in Figure 6a.

claim: mRNA levels correlate with S7p (Spearman's correlation coefficient 0.49).
source: We find that mRNA levels are most strongly correlated with S2p levels at TES of active genes (Spearman's correlation coefficient 0.62), followed by promoter K7ac (0.55) and S7p (0.49; Figure 6a).
evidence: Determined by correlation analysis shown in Figure 6a.

claim: The enrichment levels of K7me1 and K7me2 at gene promoters poorly correlate with S2p or mRNA (0.31–0.45).
source: In contrast, the enrichment levels of K7me1 and K7me2 at gene promoters (which are highly self-correlated, 0.93) poorly correlate with S2p or mRNA (0.31–0.45), but highly correlate with modifications associated with initiation and early elongation (unphosphorylated RNAPII, S5p and S7p; 0.72–0.86).
evidence: Determined by correlation analysis shown in Figure 6a.

claim: K7me1 and K7me2 highly correlate with modifications associated with initiation and early elongation (unphosphorylated RNAPII, S5p and S7p; 0.72–0.86).
source: In contrast, the enrichment levels of K7me1 and K7me2 at gene promoters (which are highly self-correlated, 0.93) poorly correlate with S2p or mRNA (0.31–0.45), but highly correlate with modifications associated with initiation and early elongation (unphosphorylated RNAPII, S5p and S7p; 0.72–0.86).
evidence: Determined by correlation analysis shown in Figure 6a.

claim: The partial correlation between K7me2 and S2p becomes zero after removing individual contributions of S5p or K7ac.
source: Surprisingly, we found that the partial correlation between K7me2 and S2p becomes zero after removing individual contributions of S5p or K7ac; similar results were obtained for K7me1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: Determined by partial correlation analysis shown in Figure 6b.

claim: Removing the contribution of S7p alone, or the combined contributions of S7p, S5p and K7ac, results in small negative correlations of K7me2 with S2p.
source: Moreover, removing the contribution of S7p alone, or the combined contributions of S7p, S5p and K7ac, results in small negative correlations of K7me2 (and K7me1) with S2p (Figure 6—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: Determined by partial correlation analysis shown in Figure 6b.

claim: K7me1 and K7me2 are anti-correlated with S2p.
source: These results suggest that K7me1 and K7me2 are anti-correlated with S2p, which in turn is highly correlated with K7ac.
evidence: Inferred from partial correlation analyses shown in Figure 6b.

claim: Both S7p and K7ac maintain positive partial correlations with S2p levels (0.29 and 0.25 respectively).
source: Both marks maintain positive partial correlations with S2p levels (0.29 and 0.25 respectively; Figure 6c), suggesting that both S7p and K7ac have direct links to the extent of elongation.
evidence: Determined by partial correlation analysis shown in Figure 6c.

claim: S7p and K7ac have direct links to the extent of elongation.
source: Both marks maintain positive partial correlations with S2p levels (0.29 and 0.25 respectively; Figure 6c), suggesting that both S7p and K7ac have direct links to the extent of elongation.
evidence: Inferred from partial correlation analysis shown in Figure 6c.

claim: S7p and K7ac are the best predictors of S2p in single-variable models.
source: These analyses confirm that S7p and K7ac are (i) the best predictors of S2p in single-variable models, (ii) the top combination of modifications in two-variable models, and (iii) always present in the top models when considering three, four and five modifications.
evidence: Determined by stepwise regression analysis shown in Figure 6d.

claim: The promoter levels of K7me1 and K7me2 have significant negative contributions to the S2p elongation mark and mRNA expression.
source: Surprisingly, we also find that the promoter levels of K7me1 and K7me2 have significant negative contributions to the S2p elongation mark and mRNA expression, when considered together with the positively correlated variables S5p, S7p and/or K7ac.
evidence: Determined by stepwise regression analysis shown in Figure 6d.

claim: The K7me2/K7ac ratio negatively correlates with mRNA expression (Spearman's correlation coefficient -0.35).
source: We find that the K7me2/K7ac ratio negatively correlates with mRNA expression (Spearman's correlation coefficient -0.35; Figure 7a, Figure 7—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: Determined by correlation analysis shown in Figure 7a.

claim: The K7me2/K7ac ratio negatively correlates with nascent transcription (correlation coefficient –0.31).
source: Analyses of nascent transcription using published GRO-seq (global run-on sequencing) data (Jonkers et al., 2014) yield a similar negative correlation with coefficient –0.31 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: Determined by analysis of GRO-seq data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1b.

claim: Genes with the highest K7me2/K7ac ratios exhibit the lowest mRNA or nascent transcript expression.
source: Interestingly, genes with the highest K7me2/K7ac ratios exhibit the lowest mRNA or nascent transcript expression (Figure 7c and 7d), and lowest S2p in the beginning of gene bodies (Figure 7c) and after TES (Figure 7d).
evidence: Demonstrated by heatmap and boxplot analyses in Figure 7c and 7d.

claim: Genes with high K7me2/K7ac ratios are associated with GO terms that relate with negative regulation of translation.
source: Interestingly, we found that genes with high K7me2/K7ac ratios are associated with GO terms that relate with negative regulation of translation, and kinase cascades, such as positive regulation of peptidyl-serine phosphorylation, of Rab GTPase activity and of JUN kinase activity.
evidence: Determined by Gene Ontology analysis shown in Figure 7e.

claim: Genes with low K7me2/K7ac ratios are associated with GO terms that relate with housekeeping functions in mouse ES cells such as translation, DNA-dependent transcription, carbohydrate utilization and regulation of developmental process.
source: In contrast, genes with low K7me2/K7ac ratios are associated with GO terms that relate with housekeeping functions in mouse ES cells such as translation, DNA-dependent transcription, carbohydrate utilization and regulation of developmental process.
evidence: Determined by Gene Ontology analysis shown in Figure 7e.

claim: Genes with high K7me2/K7ac ratio are more likely to be upregulated upon TSA treatment than downregulated.
source: We find that TSA has different effects on the three groups of genes according to their K7me2/K7ac ratio (Figure 7f). The genes with high K7me2/K7ac ratio are more likely to be upregulated (107/141 genes) upon TSA treatment, than downregulated (34/141 genes).
evidence: Determined by analysis of published microarray data shown in Figure 7f.

claim: Genes with the lowest K7me2/K7ac ratio are most often downregulated upon TSA treatment than upregulated.
source: Finally, genes with the lowest ratio are most often downregulated (142/180 genes) than upregulated (38/180 genes).
evidence: Determined by analysis of published microarray data shown in Figure 7f.

claim: Inhibition of P300 induces an average 1.7-fold increase in the global levels of K7me2.
source: We find that inhibition of P300 induces an average 1.7-fold increase in the global levels of K7me2 (ranging from 1.2 to 2.5-fold across replicates), whereas the levels of total RPB1 remain constant or are slightly increased (Figure 7g).
evidence: Demonstrated by western blot analysis after C646 treatment shown in Figure 7g.

claim: Levels of S7p remain constant after P300 inhibition with C646.
source: Levels of S7p also remain constant after P300 inhibition with C646 suggesting that K7ac and S7p contribute independently to productive elongation (Figure 7g), an observation which is consistent with the non-redundant contributions of K7ac and S7p to S2p and mRNA levels found by partial correlation and stepwise regression analyses (Figure 6).
evidence: Demonstrated by western blot analysis after C646 treatment shown in Figure 7g.

claim: K7ac and S7p contribute independently to productive elongation.
source: Levels of S7p also remain constant after P300 inhibition with C646 suggesting that K7ac and S7p contribute independently to productive elongation (Figure 7g), an observation which is consistent with the non-redundant contributions of K7ac and S7p to S2p and mRNA levels found by partial correlation and stepwise regression analyses (Figure 6).
evidence: Inferred from C646 treatment data in Figure 7g and correlation analyses in Figure 6.

claim: Serine-5 and Serine-7 phosphorylation mark transcription initiation.
source: Serine-5 and Serine-7 phosphorylation mark transcription initiation, whereas Serine-2 phosphorylation coincides with productive elongation.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Serine-2 phosphorylation coincides with productive elongation.
source: Serine-5 and Serine-7 phosphorylation mark transcription initiation, whereas Serine-2 phosphorylation coincides with productive elongation.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: The CTD has eight non-canonical substitutions of Serine-7 into Lysine-7 in vertebrates.
source: In vertebrates, the CTD has eight non-canonical substitutions of Serine-7 into Lysine-7, which can be acetylated (K7ac).
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by Figure 1.

claim: K7me1 and K7me2 are observed during the earliest transcription stages and precede or accompany Serine-5 and Serine-7 phosphorylation.
source: K7me1 and K7me2 are observed during the earliest transcription stages and precede or accompany Serine-5 and Serine-7 phosphorylation.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: K7ac is associated with RNAPII elongation, Serine-2 phosphorylation and mRNA expression.
source: In contrast, K7ac is associated with RNAPII elongation, Serine-2 phosphorylation and mRNA expression.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 5, 6, and 7.

claim: There is a balance between RNAPII K7 methylation and acetylation at gene promoters, which fine-tunes gene expression levels.
source: We identify an unexpected balance between RNAPII K7 methylation and acetylation at gene promoters, which fine-tunes gene expression levels.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 7.

claim: The CTD is a large, structurally disordered domain composed of a tandem heptapeptide repeat structure with the canonical sequence Y1-S2-P3-T4-S5-P6-S7.
source: The CTD is a large, structurally disordered domain composed of a tandem heptapeptide repeat structure with the canonical sequence Y1-S2-P3-T4-S5-P6-S7.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: RNAPII binds to promoter regions in a hypophosphorylated state.
source: RNAPII binds to promoter regions in a hypophosphorylated state, before the CTD becomes phosphorylated at Serine-5 (S5p) and Serine-7 (S7p), marking the earliest stages of transcription (Akhtar et al., 2009; Chapman et al., 2007; Tietjen et al., 2010).
evidence: Stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Productive elongation is characterized by an increase in phosphorylation of Serine-2 (S2p) throughout gene bodies, with the highest levels found around transcription end sites (TES).
source: Productive elongation is characterized by an increase in phosphorylation of Serine-2 (S2p) throughout gene bodies, with the highest levels found around transcription end sites (TES).
evidence: Stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: S5p is important for recruitment of the capping machinery.
source: S5p is important for recruitment of the capping machinery, while S2p is involved in the recruitment of splicing and polyadenylation factors (Corden, 2013; Ghosh et al., 2011; Gu et al., 2013; Lunde et al., 2010).
evidence: Stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: S2p is involved in the recruitment of splicing and polyadenylation factors.
source: S5p is important for recruitment of the capping machinery, while S2p is involved in the recruitment of splicing and polyadenylation factors (Corden, 2013; Ghosh et al., 2011; Gu et al., 2013; Lunde et al., 2010).
evidence: Stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The most complex multicellular organisms, such as vertebrates, generally have longer CTDs (e.g. 52 heptad repeats in mammals).
source: The most complex multicellular organisms, such as vertebrates, generally have longer CTDs (e.g. 52 heptad repeats in mammals), whereas Drosophila melanogaster, Caenorhabditis elegans and unicellular yeast have 44, 42 and 26–29 copies, respectively.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Drosophila melanogaster has 44 heptad repeats in its CTD.
source: The most complex multicellular organisms, such as vertebrates, generally have longer CTDs (e.g. 52 heptad repeats in mammals), whereas Drosophila melanogaster, Caenorhabditis elegans and unicellular yeast have 44, 42 and 26–29 copies, respectively.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Caenorhabditis elegans has 42 heptad repeats in its CTD.
source: The most complex multicellular organisms, such as vertebrates, generally have longer CTDs (e.g. 52 heptad repeats in mammals), whereas Drosophila melanogaster, Caenorhabditis elegans and unicellular yeast have 44, 42 and 26–29 copies, respectively.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Unicellular yeast has 26–29 heptad repeats in its CTD.
source: The most complex multicellular organisms, such as vertebrates, generally have longer CTDs (e.g. 52 heptad repeats in mammals), whereas Drosophila melanogaster, Caenorhabditis elegans and unicellular yeast have 44, 42 and 26–29 copies, respectively.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The mammalian CTD retains a core of 21 consensus repeats.
source: The mammalian CTD retains a core of 21 consensus repeats, but has accumulated a diversity of non-consensus repeats, particularly at its most C-terminal region (Figure 1a).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 1a.

claim: In vertebrates, non-canonical amino-acid residues occur most frequently at the seventh position of the heptapeptide repeat.
source: In vertebrates, non-canonical amino-acid residues occur most frequently at the seventh position of the heptapeptide repeat, and the most frequent substitution replaces the canonical S7 residue with a lysine (K7; Figure 1a).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 1a.

claim: The most frequent non-canonical substitution in vertebrate CTD replaces the canonical S7 residue with a lysine (K7).
source: In vertebrates, non-canonical amino-acid residues occur most frequently at the seventh position of the heptapeptide repeat, and the most frequent substitution replaces the canonical S7 residue with a lysine (K7; Figure 1a).
evidence: Stated in text and shown in Figure 1a.

claim: Viability of cells expressing α-amanitin-resistant RPB1 was previously shown for K7-to-R7 mutations.
source: Viability of cells expressing α-amanitin-resistant RPB1 was previously shown for K7-to-R7 mutations (Schroeder et al., 2013) or for other CTD constructs without all lysines, where Rpb1 contained only consensus heptapeptide repeats (Chapman et al., 2005; Hintermair et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: Methylation of a single CTD-R7 is involved in expression of snRNAs and snoRNAs in mammalian cells.
source: In mammalian cells, methylation of a single CTD-R7 is involved in expression of snRNAs and snoRNAs (Sims et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior published work.

claim: Conservation of CTD-K7 methylation suggests functional relevance of this modification across taxa.
source: Conservation of CTD-K7 methylation, and expansion of the number of methylated CTD-K7 residues from invertebrates to mammals, suggests functional relevance of this modification across taxa.
evidence: Inferred from the conservation data presented in Figures 1 and 3.

claim: K7me1 and K7me2 foci are sparser than the discrete nucleoplasmic domains containing total YFP-RPB1 or S5p.
source: The K7me1 and K7me2 foci are sparser than the discrete nucleoplasmic domains containing total YFP-RPB1 or S5p (see Figure 2c), consistent with their presence at RNAPII complexes involved in more restricted transcription events, rather than extensively marking chromatin-free RPB1.
evidence: Inferred from comparison of immunofluorescence patterns in Figures 2c and 4c.

claim: K7me1 and K7me2 are present at RNAPII complexes involved in more restricted transcription events, rather than extensively marking chromatin-free RPB1.
source: The K7me1 and K7me2 foci are sparser than the discrete nucleoplasmic domains containing total YFP-RPB1 or S5p (see Figure 2c), consistent with their presence at RNAPII complexes involved in more restricted transcription events, rather than extensively marking chromatin-free RPB1.
evidence: Inferred from immunofluorescence data in Figures 2c and 4c.

claim: K7me1 and K7me2 are not enriched at the secondary 8WG16 peak +140 bp downstream of the TSS.
source: K7me1 and K7me2 are enriched at the TSS-centered peak, but not at the secondary 8WG16 peak +140 bp downstream of the TSS (Figure 7c), which has previously been associated with promoter-proximal pausing (Quinodoz et al., 2014).
evidence: Demonstrated by heatmap analysis in Figure 7c.

claim: The secondary 8WG16 peak +140 bp downstream of the TSS has been associated with promoter-proximal pausing.
source: K7me1 and K7me2 are enriched at the TSS-centered peak, but not at the secondary 8WG16 peak +140 bp downstream of the TSS (Figure 7c), which has previously been associated with promoter-proximal pausing (Quinodoz et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior published work.

claim: K7ac expands downstream of the TSS up to +500 bp, especially at genes with low K7me2/K7ac ratios.
source: In contrast, K7ac expands downstream of the TSS up to +500 bp, especially at genes with low K7me2/K7ac ratios, but without specific enrichment at the secondary 8WG16 peak.
evidence: Demonstrated by heatmap analysis in Figure 7c.

claim: The balance between K7 modifications fine-tunes gene expression levels at groups of genes with different biological functions.
source: These results suggest that the balance between K7 methylation and acetylation at gene promoters is important to define the extent of productive transcription at groups of genes with different biological functions, namely in the transition between initiation and elongation, which can contribute to fine-tuning gene expression levels.
evidence: Inferred from GO analysis and K7me2/K7ac ratio analyses shown in Figure 7.

claim: The effect of TSA on the three groups of genes (high, medium, low K7me2/K7ac ratio) is significantly different (Fisher's exact test; high versus low ratio: p < 2.2x10–16).
source: The effect of TSA on three groups of genes is significantly different (Fisher's exact test; high versus low ratio: p < 2.2x10–16).
evidence: Determined by statistical analysis of TSA treatment data shown in Figure 7f.
